<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]], [[Minsk Protocol]]
**[[Ukraine]] agrees to the "Steinmeier formula", aimed at granting a special [[Self-governance|self-governing]] status to the [[Donbass]] and organising [[Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe|OSCE]]-validated elections according to [[Law of Ukraine|Ukrainian law]]. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/ukraine-agrees-to-steinmeier-formula-green-lights-elections-in-occupied-donbas.html (''Kyiv Post'')] [https://tass.com/world/1080822 (TASS)]
*[[2015–19 Iraqi protests]], [[2018–19 Arab protests|New Arab Spring]]
**At least two people are killed and 200 are injured at protests against unemployment and government corruption in [[Iraq]]. Protestors also try to enter the fortified [[Green Zone]] in [[Baghdad]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-protests/iraqi-police-open-fire-use-tear-gas-and-water-cannon-to-disperse-baghdad-protests-idUSKBN1WG44U (Reuters)]
*[[Northern Mali conflict]]
**[[Mali]]'s government says jihadist militant attacks on [[Malian Armed Forces|military]] (FAMA) posts in [[Mondoro]] and Boulkessi, in the central [[Mopti Region]], killed 41 troops and left 60 others missing, possibly captured, while also inflicting heavy equipment losses. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/mali-says-25-soldiers-killed-in-attacks-by-suspected-jihadists-idUSKBN1WG4U4 (Reuters)] [https://www.dw.com/en/mali-dozens-killed-and-missing-in-attack-on-army-camps/a-50670119 (Deutsche Welle)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-10-12/worst-jihadist-attack-in-years-stokes-anger-over-mali-s-response (Bloomberg)]
*[[2019–2020 Hong Kong protests]]
**An 18-year-old protestor is shot in the chest by police and taken to hospital for surgery during clashes between pro-democracy protesters and the police in [[Hong Kong]] on [[National Day of the People's Republic of China]]. Video footage shows the police officer shooting the protester as  the protester tries to hit his arm with a metal pipe. This is the first reported injury from a live round.  [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-49891403 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[70th anniversary of the People's Republic of China]]
**[[China]] celebrates its [[National Day of the People's Republic of China|National Day]] with parades across the country, including a large military parade in the capital [[Beijing]]. [https://www.cnn.com/asia/live-news/china-hong-kong-oct-1-live-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]

;Business and economy
*[[Belfast]] shipyard [[Harland and Wolff]] owner [[Dolphin Drilling]] announces it has found a buyer for the shipyard, infrastructure-based InfraStrata, saving it from closure. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-harlandandwolff-m-a-infrastrata/belfasts-harland-and-wolff-shipyard-saved-in-6-million-pound-infrastrata-deal-idUSKBN1WG31O (Reuters)]
*[[United Parcel Service]] announces that it has been designated as the first official, commercial, drone airline service by the [[Federal Aviation Administration]]. [https://www.wired.com/story/ups-drone-airline-faa-certification-delivery/?itm_campaign=TechinTwo (''Wired'')]
*In leaked audio from a meeting with employees in July, [[Facebook]] CEO [[Mark Zuckerberg]] threatens to sue Senator [[Elizabeth Warren]], who is running in the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 U.S. presidential election]], if she is elected president and tries to "break up" [[Big Four tech companies|large tech]] companies. [https://www.theverge.com/2019/10/1/20756701/mark-zuckerberg-facebook-leak-audio-ftc-antitrust-elizabeth-warren-tiktok-comments (''The Verge'')]
* [[Kristalina Georgieva]] succeeds [[Christine Lagarde]] as the Managing Director of the [[International Monetary Fund]]. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/imfs-new-chief-vows-to-fix-the-roof-before-the-storm-hits-11570096800 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
;Disasters and accidents
*The [[Nanfang'ao Bridge]], the only steel single-arch bridge in [[Taiwan]], collapses on fishing boats in [[Su'ao]]. Ten people are injured and six are believed to have been trapped. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-taiwan-bridge/taiwan-bridge-collapse-crushes-fishing-boats-six-crew-feared-trapped-idUSKBN1WG2P3 (Reuters)]
*Severe flooding affects [[Laxey]], [[Isle of Man]], with some residents evacuated from their homes. [http://www.isleofman.com/news/video/87780/floods-old-laxey (Isle of Man Government)]

;Health and environment
*[[Climate change mitigation]]
**[[Dutch people|Dutch]] farmers stage a protest in [[The Hague]] against proposals to halve livestock numbers in a bid to cut [[Nitrogen oxide emissions|nitrogen emissions]]. Motoring group ANWB claims tractors on highways caused a total of 1,136km (700 miles) of [[traffic jam]]s during morning rush hour, with tractors on one highway swerving back and forth to prevent traffic passing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-49891449 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–United States relations]], [[List of North Korean missile tests|North Korean missile tests]], [[Japan–North Korea relations]]
**[[North Korea]] says it will resume working-level nuclear talks with the [[United States]], reviving a denuclearization process that has remained stalled since a February summit in [[Vietnam]] ended without a deal. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/u-s-and-north-korea-to-resume-nuclear-talks-pyongyang-says-11569927143?fbclid=IwAR2RG7m2WrWVARmUxIDfNMPD1yUpO-WVew_Pfz7HIiBwhidd0jnARsA-EBA (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
**[[North Korea]] fires a missile which lands in the [[exclusive economic zone of Japan]], according to [[Japan]]ese [[Chief Cabinet Secretary]] [[Yoshihide Suga]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-missiles-japan-suga/one-north-korea-missile-fell-into-japans-eez-japan-government-idUSKBN1WG4ZP (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Kuopio school stabbing]]
**A woman is killed and ten other people injured when a student attacks a teacher and students with a sword at a [[vocational school]] inside a [[shopping mall]] in [[Kuopio]], [[Northern Savonia]], [[Finland]]. Police disarm and arrest the suspect, who is one of the injured. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/world/finland-shooting-one-dead-and-nine-injured-at-school-in-kuopio-shopping-centre-a4251016.html (''Evening Standard'')] [https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/01/europe/violent-incident-finland-dead-intl/index.html (CNN)] [https://newsnowfinland.fi/crime/developing-1-dead-10-injured-in-kuopio-college-sword-attack (NewsNow)]
*A jury finds Amber Guyger, a former [[Dallas Police Department|Dallas police officer]], guilty of murder. Guyger was indicted last year after fatally shooting her unarmed neighbor, [[Botham Jean]], in his own apartment, which she claims to have mistaken for her own. [https://amp.sacbee.com/news/nation-world/national/article235659352.html?fbclid=IwAR0NmUNEbg68IBJU_aY5rPIvbueaRJpDmlWtmCGP16IRR1_THj803gFnbvI (''The Sacramento Bee'')]
*A [[United States district court|U.S. district judge]] in [[Boston]], [[Massachusetts]], upholds [[Harvard University]]'s admissions process following a challenge from a group of [[Asian Americans|Asian American]] applicants who believe the school discriminated against them. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/01/politics/harvard-affirmative-action/index.html?utm_source=CNN-News-Alerts&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=Federal+judge+upholds+Harvard (CNN)]
*In the [[United Kingdom]], [[Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex|Prince Harry]] and [[Meghan, Duchess of Sussex|Meghan Markle]] announce they are suing ''[[The Mail on Sunday]]'', as well as its parent company [[DMG Media]], claiming the publisher's newspapers have been publishing "false and deliberately derogatory stories" about their lives. [https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/meghan-markle-prince-harry-legal-action-mail-on-sunday-dad-letter-193755627.html (Yahoo! News)]
*[[Opioid epidemic in the United States]]
**[[Johnson & Johnson]] announces it has reached a $20.4 million settlement with two [[Ohio]] counties over its role in the [[opioid epidemic in the United States]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/investigations/johnson-and-johnson-reaches-tentative-204-million-settlement-in-massive-opioid-case/2019/10/01/6a8a9670-e48e-11e9-b403-f738899982d2_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*Aida Merlano, a former [[Colombian Congress|Congresswoman]] who is serving a fifteen-year sentence for buying votes and for firearms offences, escapes from prison in [[Bogotá]], [[Colombia]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/colombia-politician-prison-break-rope-motorbike-dentist-aida-merlano-bogota-a9136916.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[2019 Trump–Ukraine scandal]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s personal lawyer [[Rudy Giuliani]] hires [[Watergate scandal]] prosecutor Jon Sale to represent him in the impeachment inquiry investigating the president. [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/10/01/trump-lawyer-rudy-giuliani-hires-attorney-jon-sale-to-represent-him.html?fbclid=IwAR037r76qHk_OcD1gdm-UAJABKkhGTE3pj1MFCb8JrKZtv08nIdsIfMQTLM (CNBC)]
**[[Steve Linick]], the [[Office of the Inspector General of the Department of State|inspector general of the U.S. State Department]], requests an "urgent" briefing with senior congressional staff members regarding [[Ukraine]]. The private meeting will be held tomorrow. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/01/politics/deposition-delayed-impeachment-investigation/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Immigration policy of the first Donald Trump administration|Immigration policy of Donald Trump]]
**''[[The New York Times]]'' reports that [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] suggested shooting migrants in the legs in order to slow them down after they crossed the [[Mexico–United States border]] during a meeting in March. He also reportedly suggested digging a moat to fortify a [[Mexico–United States barrier|border wall]] and filling it with "snakes or alligators", and wanted the wall "electrified, with spikes on top that could pierce human flesh". [https://www.businessinsider.com/trump-suggested-shooting-migrants-in-legs-border-moat-2019-10?fbclid=IwAR0ppcLU0wSHa9UpSmq_7_REJyE-RfU1_QJLbNyA4VdWd7dyZsyURfefSBs (''Business Insider'')]
*[[Tax returns of Donald Trump]]
**A U.S. federal judge in [[California]] blocks a state law requiring presidential candidates to disclose income [[tax return|tax returns]] before their names can appear on the state's [[United States presidential primary|primary]] ballot. The ruling is considered a win for [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], who has resisted releasing his tax returns. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/01/politics/california-law-trump-tax-returns-blocked/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Impeachment inquiry into Donald Trump]]
**[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] accuses [[United States House of Representatives|House]] [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] of attempting to "intimidate" and "bully" five [[United States State Department|State Department]] officials whom key congressional committees have asked to interview as part of an [[impeachment]] inquiry into [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]. The House Democrats in turn issue a warning to Pompeo to stop "intimidating" witnesses, telling Pompeo that it "is illegal and will constitute evidence of obstruction of the impeachment inquiry" into President Trump. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/pompeo-accuses-house-democrats-intimidate-bully-state-department/story (ABC News)], [https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/01/politics/pompeo-accuses-democrats-intimidation/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2019 Peruvian constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Vice President of Peru]] [[Mercedes Aráoz]], who was named by the [[Congress of Peru|Congress]] as the acting [[President of Peru|president]], resigns from both offices to facilitate the snap general election. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-49901872 (BBC News)]
*[[Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign]]
**The [[Republican National Committee]] and the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 U.S. presidential election]] campaign to reelect [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] raised $125 million between July and September, setting a new presidential fundraising record, the [[Associated Press]] reports. [https://www.axios.com/trumps-reelection-effort-raised-125-million-d65fbdbb-6e0d-43ca-a7ba-bc04792c992e.html (''Axios'')]
*[[Politics of San Marino]]
**[[Luca Boschi]] and [[Mariella Mularoni]] begins the term as [[List of Captains Regent of San Marino|Captain Regents]]. [https://sanmarinortv.sm/news/politica-c2/san-marino-saluta-i-nuovi-capitani-reggenti-per-il-semestre-10-ottobre-2019-10-aprile-2020-a177695 (San Marino TV)]
